newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland may free hard coal prices in 1997 - minister.
newsitem.headline: Poland may free hard coal prices in 1997 - minister.

text.p: Poland may free prices of hard coal, the country's main source of energy, in 1997 to help ailing mines, Economy Minister Wieslaw Kaczmarek said on Tuesday.

"We should analyse the coal price policy. In 1997 long-term agreements between mines and the energy sector will expire. Bringing the (coal) prices to market level could thus take place," Kaczmarek told a news conference.
He did not elaborate on the move, which some analysts say would lift electricity prices and create a strong inflationary impulse.
Mines which had a net loss of 1.4 billion zlotys last year and whose debt has piled to about nine billion zloty, said their problems result from official caps on coal prices.

But most analysts said they were in the red because the government keeps delaying, for political reasons, a restructuring programme that would involve radical job cuts the closure of unprofitable pits.
